# truefoundry_gateway_load_balancing_config (Resource)

Manages the AI gateway load balancing configuration: which target models matching requests are spread over, and how. Applied as a `gateway-load-balancing-config` manifest via `PUT /api/svc/v1/apply`. Unlike the `routing` block of a `virtual-model` in `truefoundry_provider_account`, these rules route requests that address a real model, without a virtual model in front of it. **The load balancing config is a tenant-wide singleton** — define at most one of this resource per control plane; an apply replaces all rules. Import the existing config with `terraform import truefoundry_gateway_load_balancing_config.example gateway-load-balancing-config`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The tenant-wide AI gateway load balancing config (singleton — define at most
# one): which target models matching requests are spread over, and how.
#
# Unlike the `routing` block of a virtual model, these rules route requests
# that address a real model, without a virtual model in front of it.
resource "truefoundry_gateway_load_balancing_config" "routing" {
  name = "load-balancing-config"

  rules = [
    # 70/30 split of one model across two regions, with the second region also
    # taking over when the first rate-limits.
    {
      id   = "gpt-4o-regions"
      type = "weight-based-routing"

      when = {
        models = ["my-azure-openai-francecentral/gpt-4o"]
      }

      load_balance_targets = [
        {
          target = "my-azure-openai-francecentral/gpt-4o"
          weight = 70
        },
        {
          target                = "my-azure-openai-swedencentral/gpt-4o"
          weight                = 30
          fallback_status_codes = ["429", "503"]
          fallback_candidate    = true
        },
      ]
    },

    # An ordered fallback chain for one team: priority 0 is tried first.
    {
      id   = "team-fallback-chain"
      type = "priority-based-routing"

      when = {
        subjects = ["team:everyone"]
      }

      load_balance_targets = [
        { target = "my-azure-openai-francecentral/gpt-4.1", priority = 0 },
        { target = "my-azure-openai-swedencentral/gpt-4.1", priority = 1 },
      ]
    },

    # Everything else goes to whichever target is currently fastest.
    {
      id   = "fastest-wins"
      type = "latency-based-routing"
      when = {}

      load_balance_targets = [
        {
          target = "my-azure-openai-francecentral/gpt-4o-mini"

          headers_override = {
            set = { "x-routed-by" = "terraform" }
          }
        },
        { target = "my-azure-openai-swedencentral/gpt-4o-mini" },
      ]
    },
  ]
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the load balancing config (3-32 characters, lowercase alphanumeric and hyphens).
- `rules` (Attributes Set) Load balancing rules, normally scoped so that at most one matches a given request. This is a set: the order rules are written in carries no meaning, and which rule wins when several match is up to the control plane. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rules))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Control plane ID of the gateway load balancing config.

<a id="nestedatt--rules"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rules`

Required:

- `id` (String) Identifier of this rule, unique within the config. 2-62 characters of letters, digits, and hyphens; must start with a letter and end with a letter or digit.
- `load_balance_targets` (Attributes Set) Target models matching requests are routed to. The control plane rejects targets that do not exist. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rules--load_balance_targets))
- `type` (String) Routing strategy. One of: `weight-based-routing`, `latency-based-routing`, `priority-based-routing`. `weight-based-routing` needs a `weight` on every target, `priority-based-routing` a `priority`; `latency-based-routing` takes neither and picks the fastest target. The control plane ignores a `weight` or `priority` its strategy does not use, so this provider rejects that combination at plan time rather than applying a value that has no effect.
- `when` (Attributes) Requests this rule applies to; all given parts must match. An empty block (`{}`) matches every request. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rules--when))

<a id="nestedatt--rules--load_balance_targets"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rules.load_balance_targets`

Required:

- `target` (String) Target model as `<provider-account>/<model-name>`.

Optional:

- `fallback_candidate` (Boolean) Whether this target may serve as a fallback for other targets.
- `fallback_status_codes` (Set of String) Status codes for which the request falls back to other targets.
- `headers_override` (Attributes) Headers to remove from or set on the upstream request for this target. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rules--load_balance_targets--headers_override))
- `metadata_match` (Map of String) Metadata key-value pairs that must match incoming request metadata headers for this target to be considered.
- `priority` (Number) Priority of the target; 0 is highest (priority-based routing).
- `weight` (Number) Relative routing weight; higher values receive more traffic (weight-based routing).

<a id="nestedatt--rules--load_balance_targets--headers_override"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rules.load_balance_targets.headers_override`

Optional:

- `remove` (Set of String) Headers to remove from the upstream request.
- `set` (Map of String) Headers to add or overwrite on the upstream request.



<a id="nestedatt--rules--when"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rules.when`

Optional:

- `metadata` (Map of String) Request metadata key-value pairs to match, from the `X-TFY-METADATA` header.
- `models` (Set of String) Models to match, as `<provider-account>/<model>` names.
- `subjects` (Set of String) Subject FQNs to match, e.g. `user:someone@example.com` or `team:everyone`. The control plane rejects subjects that do not exist.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The load balancing config is a tenant-wide singleton; its import ID is the
# fixed string "gateway-load-balancing-config".
terraform import truefoundry_gateway_load_balancing_config.routing gateway-load-balancing-config
```
